title: Type-check HXX tags, props, and children in Haxe before emission
description: Review of the showcase HXX contract found that genes-ts currently parses markup and type-checks interpolated expressions but delegates the relationship between a tag and its props/children to emitted TypeScript. The planner validates tag identity, required/extra/duplicate props, direct/interpolated values, callbacks, spreads, and children before any output transaction commits; imported aliases and direct generics retain their typed identities. One validated plan feeds typed TSX, erased JSX, typed createElement, and classic JavaScript. Weak or unresolved contracts fail closed at the authored source position, while strict TypeScript remains an independent parity oracle rather than the primary checker. Provider coverage may expand through separately reviewed closed declarations; unsupported properties remain errors rather than falling back to a broad map.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Haxe compilation rejects a misspelled intrinsic tag at the original HXX source position before emitting TypeScript or JavaScript.
- Haxe compilation rejects unknown props, missing required props, wrong direct attribute/interpolation types, incompatible event handlers, invalid children, and unsound spreads against the precisely identified intrinsic or component prop contract.
- Imported and aliased component values preserve their typed prop identity; lowercase intrinsic/custom-element handling remains explicit and does not guess from capitalization alone.
- Valid intrinsic elements, generic components, optional props, boolean props, data/aria attributes, fragments, typed spreads, and children compile without redundant annotations.
- The checker uses typed Haxe declarations or a deterministic versioned declaration projection; it introduces no Dynamic, Any, untyped, cast, Reflect, broad unknown, unchecked assertion, or silent fallback. Unsupported contracts fail with an actionable source-positioned diagnostic.
- TSX and typed createElement output remain canonical and strict TypeScript stays as an independent parity oracle. Classic genes JavaScript preserves equivalent runtime behavior.
- Framework-neutral positive and exact negative fixtures cover every rule, both output profiles pass, the full genes-ts suite has no regressions, and a packed consumer proves the public authoring path.
- Any upstream PR explains that the gap was discovered while developing NextJsHx, includes before/after HXX and emitted output plus negative controls, and keeps the change fully generalized.

The same semantic plan is exercised in typed TSX, JSX-source, classic TSX, typed createElement, and classic JavaScript, with runtime differential and canonical snapshots. title: Add Haxe-native React state Hooks and move commerce cart logic out of TypeScript
description: The commerce showcase review found that its central filter/cart state is implemented in client/cart-hook.ts while Haxe only declares an extern. Use a typed Tuple2 projection for raw state, EitherType only at the raw React boundary, State<S>.value/set/update for intent, useStateLazy for possibly callable initial values, and direct-only React.deps(...) for explicit heterogeneous memo dependencies. Haxe remains the primary checker. Export explicitly marked Haxe Hooks through directive-first named const-alias adapters. Initial no-argument state supports exact undefined only because Haxe 4.3.7 overload probing showed the contextual generic form can widen to generated any. - The semantic Haxe API reduces boilerplate versus direct TypeScript tuple/union modeling and makes value updates and functional updates type-safe and discoverable without unchecked union tricks.
- Developers can author and compose a typed custom Hook entirely in Haxe, consume a typed native TS Hook from Haxe, and expose/consume a Haxe-authored Hook from TS through deterministic generated output or a minimal owned adapter.
- Common Hook use requires no redundant type annotations when Haxe can infer the state, memo value, dependencies, and callback contracts soundly.
- The commerce showcase implements its cart/filter custom Hook and state transitions in Haxe; client/cart-hook.ts is removed from that application package.
- Native TypeScript Hook interop remains covered by a dedicated, explicitly mixed interop/adoption example rather than application-core behavior.

title: Design non-deceptive Server Function security ergonomics
description:
## Decision

Select how Haxe should make public Server Function trust boundaries harder to misuse without pretending that a macro proves application authentication or authorization. Lock the boundary between mechanically provable structure and runtime application policy.

## Rationale

Every exported Server Function is reachable through a direct POST and must validate input, authenticate, authorize the exact operation and resource, and sanitize returned data. The existing typed adapter and FormData decoder make shape errors harder, but security remains advisory. Haxe can improve omission resistance with types and capabilities only if those types cannot be manufactured without executing application-provided request and resource checks.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep documentation-only guidance on each action.
- Require explicit public-action metadata without enforcing a policy flow.
- Provide decoded-input combinators and generated secure skeletons.
- Require application-provided verifier callbacks that produce scoped authorization witnesses consumed by protected services.
- Statically search action bodies for decoder or auth calls; this risks false security and must not be selected unless a sound reduced contract exists.
- Replace native Server Functions with custom RPC middleware; this is rejected by architecture.
design: Selected GuardedAction.run with one inferred config: closed decode; per-invocation request authentication; authenticated target resolution; exact operation authorization; private immutable Authorized<Operation, Actor, Target, Input>; mutation; coarse rejection mapping; mandatory DomainResult-to-PublicResult projection. Raw @:next.action remains native transport and receives no security classification. Missing and denied collapse to Unavailable. Static enforcement is limited to stage presence/order, witness construction, transport exclusion, and final serialization; session, tenancy, policy, transaction, and disclosure correctness remain application-owned. Native Next POST/origin/body/action-ID behavior is documented and not reimplemented.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision separates mechanically provable facts (closed input/result shape, decoder use, graph edge, server-only dependencies) from application facts that require runtime evidence (identity, authorization, tenancy, ownership).
- At least two realistic mutation examples compare the current API with candidate Haxe APIs and show positive, unauthenticated, unauthorized, malformed-input, and overexposed-result behavior.
- The selected design cannot confer an Authorized type or equivalent without executing an application-provided verifier for the current request and resource.
- Native Next origin checks, body-size configuration, action IDs, and direct POST reachability are represented accurately and are not reimplemented.
- Any static analysis admits its blind spots and cannot be silenced with a broad annotation or cast.
- If a genuinely unresolved macro/security tradeoff remains after reduced fixtures, an Oracle GPT-5.6 Pro prompt and sanitized Repomix ZIP are prepared for user upload before implementation.
notes: Decision evidence added in ADR 0005 with create-workspace and toggle-resource positive/negative controls, malformed/unauthenticated/unauthorized/missing/overexposed behavior, useActionState trust warning, and implementation evidence matrix. Architecture index, architecture reference, PRD, Server Function guide, and architecture-doc gate updated. Verified: npm run test:architecture; npm run test:security-tooling; npm run lint:whitespace; Python bytecode compile; focused trailing-whitespace scan. Oracle review not needed because the boundary reduced to an ordinary typed pipeline and existing private-constructor pattern; implementation still requires compiler/runtime/Next/browser evidence.
close_reason: Accepted and documented the non-deceptive guarded Server Function security contract with exact guarantees, non-guarantees, examples, and executable documentation gate.

title: Lock the Haxe-native Server/Client Component authoring contract
description:
## Decision

Select the durable Haxe-native Server/Client Component authoring contract before changing macros. Lock how reusable Server Components, Client Component entrypoints, neutral shared definitions, third-party client wrappers, async server render, children and slots, Suspense/error composition, and native TypeScript interop are declared and consumed.

## Rationale

The current explicit clientComponent(path) plus ClientComponent.ref model safely preserves the Next graph, but generated adapter placement and ref ceremony leak implementation mechanics into application code. React also defines server/client at the module usage graph rather than as a nominal component class, so a simpler API must not create a false permanent environment type or weaken independent Next checks.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep explicit adapter paths and refs as the primary API.
- Infer adapter targets and expose discoverable typed companions while retaining native generated adapters.
- Emit boundaries directly from genes-ts instead of using narrow host adapters.
- Add a custom component runtime or nominal ServerComponent/ClientComponent hierarchy; this is expected to be rejected because it would misrepresent React semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- An ADR amendment or new ADR compares explicit paths/refs, inferred companions, and direct compiler emission with representative Haxe and generated TSX.
- The selected syntax keeps Server Components implicit by default, makes client entry intent explicit, and hides generated adapter placement from ordinary application code.
- The design explains reusable component usage in both server and client graphs without incorrectly assigning one permanent environment to a neutral definition.
- Third-party client-only libraries, children/slots, async server renders, Suspense, error boundaries, and native TypeScript imports have exact authoring examples.
- Positive and negative examples show what improves over plain Next.js and what remains a Next build responsibility.
- Migration and raw escape behavior are documented; no custom React runtime or broad type is proposed.

A macro field injected onto an @:build component is invalid in Haxe, while a static extension macro preserves the consuming class context and supports the selected `TideDial.client()` syntax. title: Implement serialized Haxe watch plus next dev orchestration
description:
Provide the daily dev loop while leaving HMR and runtime ownership to Next.

Planning alias: NXHX-T07
PRD sections: 15.4
design:
## Selected direction

Expose one daily command: `nextjshx dev [--config <path>] [-- <next dev arguments>]`. The CLI owns Haxe compilation and generated-output publication lifecycle; Next.js owns the application server, Turbopack or webpack, Fast Refresh, and runtime behavior. Do not add a parallel HMR protocol or runtime.

Use a serialized dirty-loop state machine rather than starting one compile per filesystem event: idle -> compiling, record dirty while compiling, then run exactly one coalesced follow-up against the newest filesystem state. Compile and render in private transaction state and publish only a complete successful plan through the existing manifest-owned journal. Unchanged generated files remain untouched so Next receives the smallest possible invalidation set.

The long-running dev command may own an isolated Haxe compilation server for its workspace and exact toolchain/build identity. One-shot generate, typecheck, build, tests, and CI remain direct and never leave a background server. Never attach to an arbitrary external `haxe --wait` process; reuse requires positive same-workspace and same-toolchain/build identity evidence. If server startup or a connection fails, report it and fall back to a bounded direct compile while attempting safe recovery. HXML, toolchain, classpath, library, resource, or NextJsHx config changes invalidate the server identity and restart it; ordinary Haxe edits reuse it.

Startup recovers an interrupted publication and performs an initial generation. If that generation fails but the existing live tree and manifest are verified last-good, keep Next running on those bytes and enter watch mode; if no verified tree exists, fail startup with the Haxe diagnostic. Next is one long-lived child. Prefix interleaved lines by source without rewriting or hiding raw compiler/framework errors. SIGINT, SIGTERM, parent exit, and child exit use bounded process-group cleanup for Next plus only the Haxe server owned by this invocation.

The read-only `haxe.elixir.codex` reference demonstrates useful patterns to retain: explicit long-running ownership, project/toolchain-scoped server state, debounce, atomic last-good promotion, bounded compatibility probes, stale-process cleanup, direct one-shot defaults, and full raw error capture. NextJsHx should improve on its watcher by making dirty-during-compile state explicit, proving no edit is lost, and keeping all publication authority in the existing transaction layer.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `nextjshx dev [--config <path>] [-- <Next dev arguments>]` is documented, rejects ambiguous or duplicate CLI input, and forwards ordinary supported `next dev` arguments byte-for-byte without a shell.
- The command recovers journaled publication state, verifies any last-good manifest/tree, performs an initial Haxe generation, and starts one long-lived `next dev` child. An initial Haxe failure may continue only with a verified last-good tree; without one it exits nonzero and does not claim a usable dev server.
- Haxe source and effective build inputs are watched: recursive HXML/classpaths, declared resources and extra inputs, `nextjshx.config.json`, `.haxerc`, and library/toolchain identity inputs. Native TS/JS/CSS watching remains owned by Next or the application package.
- Filesystem bursts are debounced and coalesced through a tested idle/compiling/dirty state machine. There is never more than one compile/publication transaction, and an edit arriving during compilation always causes one newest-state follow-up rather than being dropped.
- Only a complete successful Haxe compile, canonical plan render, syntax check, and ownership preflight can reach the existing transactional publisher. A failure leaves all live adapters and the manifest byte-identical to the last verified good generation.
- Successful publication rewrites only changed owned files, so Next/Turbopack receives normal filesystem invalidations and remains the sole HMR/Fast Refresh owner. No custom websocket, browser runtime, or Next cache mutation is introduced.
- The dev process owns an isolated Haxe server scoped to canonical workspace plus exact Haxe/lix, HXML, defines, classpath/library/resource, and genes-ts identity. Ordinary `.hx` edits reuse it; identity-changing edits restart it. Arbitrary external servers are not trusted, and bounded direct compilation is the safe fallback.
- Haxe compile failure does not kill Next. Diagnostics are source-prefixed (`haxe`, `nextjshx`, `next`, `tsc`) while preserving raw messages and source locations; a later successful compile emits one clear recovery message. Output is bounded for stored diagnostics without truncating the live stream.
- SIGINT, SIGTERM, parent exit, Next exit, Haxe-server crash, and stale prior state have deterministic tests. Cleanup terminates the owned process group/server within a deadline, never kills another workspace server, and leaves no lock, journal temporary, watcher, or orphan process.
- Focused unit/integration tests cover event bursts, dirty-during-compile, server restart/fallback, initial failure with and without last-good output, publication rollback, argument pass-through, exit-code propagation, and macOS/Linux path/process behavior.
- A real browser fixture proves edit Haxe -> rendered update via Next Fast Refresh, introduce Haxe error -> Next stays available on last-good UI, fix error -> UI updates without restarting the dev command. The test is bounded, uses zero retries beyond readiness polling, and cleans up all children.
- `nextjshx init` package-script proposals use this command idempotently once NXHX-T06 lands, and the landing, blog, commerce, and todo examples document and exercise the same daily command.

Positive example: while `nextjshx dev -- --turbopack -p 3100` is running, two rapid Haxe saves coalesce; the newest successful output is atomically published and the browser refreshes through Next.

Negative control: a syntax error during the same burst prints the original Haxe diagnostic but cannot partially replace adapters, remove the manifest, race a second publisher, or stop Next; after the fix, one queued compile publishes the recovered UI.
